growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: two long strap-shaped cotyledons, then a first pair of simple toothed leaves, then trifoliate and finally pinnate leaves. Seedlings carpet shady woodland floors; saplings are straight, thick-twigged whips with stout grey shoots, big black velvety buds, few branches and pinnate leaves of 9-13 leaflets. Ripe seed usually waits two winters (~18 months) to germinate.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Fraxinus excelsior: to 43 m; rarely >250 yr, pollards 400+; ripe brown seed dormant ~18 months (two winters), green seed germinates at once; young seedlings shade-tolerant, older trees light-demanding); Biological Flora of the British Isles (Wardle 1961); seeding from ~20-30 yr.

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (flowers open before the leaves in spring; trees male, female or mixed and may switch between years; samaras 2.5-4.5 cm, often hanging in bunches through winter); wind-pollinated tufts of dark purple naked flowers (Wardle 1961). Fruit set, rot and crop estimated.

Saplings build a zigzag stem with flat, horizontal, layered leaf sprays, persist for decades in deep shade, and keep dry brown leaves through winter.
growth.source: Wikipedia (Fagus sylvatica: 25-35 m, ~4 m at 10 yr; small seed crops from ~10 yr, heavy from ~30 yr; ~300 yr usual, >500 yr max); European silvics (very shade-tolerant, seeds overwinter and germinate in spring, masts every few years).

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (flowers with the new leaves mid-Apr to early May, wind-pollinated; seed matures 5-6 months after pollination; two 3-sided nuts 15-20 mm in a spiny cupule that splits in autumn; heavy masts after hot dry summers, rarely two years running). Fruit set, hang, rot, crop estimated.

Crop estimated.

growth.source: USDA Silvics (acorns take 2 seasons and germinate the spring after seedfall; first crop ~25 yr, abundant from 50; good crops every 2-5 yr; roots of dieback seedlings 10-15+ yr older than tops; 20-30 m at maturity); USDA FEIS (intermediate shade tolerance); lifespan estimated

The seedling shows two cotyledons, then for several years a single small, shallowly lobed umbrella leaf on a short stalk, a little larger each year as the rhizome thickens. Only mature rhizomes send up the forked, two-leaved stalk with one nodding white flower. Leaves yellow and vanish by midsummer.

growth.source: USDA FEIS species review (Hedera helix): 60-100% germination within ~15 days once pulp is removed; 3-5-lobed juvenile leaves with aerial roots vs unlobed adult leaves; ~30-40 yr to reach tree canopies, adult phase after ~10+ yr at 15-20 m; stems 50-66+ yr documented, one of 433 yr; legendary shade tolerance.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS and Wikipedia (Hedera helix: protandrous yellow-green flowers in globose umbels of 8-20, 3-5 cm across, late summer to late autumn, visited by >70 insect species, flies and wasps important late; berries 6-9 mm, black, 2-5 seeds, ripen Dec-May; bird-dispersed; somewhat poisonous).
